title: What are the next three numbers in this pattern?
description: A pattern of decimals runs from four point four to six point zero. The change between neighbours is found and checked, then added again and again to write the next three terms. Keeko's doubt adds only one tenth each time.
teaching_notes: One idea: find the change between neighbouring terms, check that it repeats, and keep adding it. Watch for students who guess a change of one tenth without taking one term from the next.

source: Find the change in 4.4, 4.8, 5.2, 5.6, 6.0 and write the nex
video_script.why: The child can add and subtract decimals and now uses them to continue a pattern.
video_script.substitution: Take each term from the next, check that the change repeats, and keep adding it to the last term.
video_script.anchor: A pattern of decimal numbers: four point four, four point eight, five point two, five point six, six point zero.
video_script.wrong_move: Adds just one tenth to the last term, instead of finding the change by taking one term from the next.
video_script.payoff_line: Find the change between neighbours, and keep adding it

final_answer.spoken: six point four, six point eight and seven point two

maths_rules: the slip: 6.0 + 0.1 = 6.1, but the change is 0.4, not 0.1
video_script.design: The five numbers sit on a number line with the same jump drawn between each pair. The jump is measured, repeated to check, then drawn three more times beyond the last number.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a row of numbers 4.4, 4.8, 5.2, 5.6, 6.0 and three empty boxes

marks.scene: the title card From your book arrives
marks.first: 4.4, 4.8 and 5.2 are written in a row
marks.more: 5.6 and 6.0 are added to the row
marks.ask: three empty boxes appear after the row

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about a pattern of decimals.
<bookmark mark='first'/>The numbers are four point four, four point eight and five point two.
<bookmark mark='more'/>Then five point six and six point zero.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>What are the next three numbers?

beats.on_screen: the row of numbers stays with the three empty boxes

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a short row of numbers with one jump drawn between two neighbours

marks.pattern: a short row of numbers appears
marks.term: one number in the row is lit and named term
marks.change: a jump arrow is drawn from one term to the next

beats.colours: the jump arrow in a new colour
narration: <bookmark mark='pattern'/>A pattern is a list of numbers that follow a rule.
<bookmark mark='term'/>Each number in the list is called a term.
<bookmark mark='change'/>The change is what we add to get from one term to the next.
<bookmark mark='start'/>Given, the pattern starts four point four, four point eight, five point two.
<bookmark mark='end'/>It goes on to five point six and six point zero.

beats.on_screen: To find: the change, and the next three terms

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the change, and the next three terms.

marks.rule: an arrow shows each term taken from the next

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, take each term away from the next term.
<bookmark mark='g1'/>Four point eight take away four point four is zero point four.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Five point two take away four point eight is zero point four.

marks.check: the words check the change repeats are written
marks.same: all four changes are boxed as 0.4

beats.colours: the four equal changes in one colour
narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step two, check that the change repeats.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>Five point six take away five point two is zero point four.
<bookmark mark='g4'/>Six point zero take away five point six is zero point four.
<bookmark mark='same'/>The change is zero point four each time.

marks.rule: an arrow runs from the last term to a new box
marks.add: 6.0 + 0.4 = 6.4 is written in the first box

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step three, add the change to the last term.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Six point zero plus zero point four is six point four.

marks.rule: arrows run to the next two boxes
marks.second: 6.4 + 0.4 = 6.8 is written in the second box
marks.third: 6.8 + 0.4 = 7.2 is written in the third box

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step four, keep adding the change.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Six point four plus zero point four is six point eight.
<bookmark mark='third'/>Six point eight plus zero point four is seven point two.

marks.payoff: the rule is written above the answer
marks.ans: the three new terms are boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='payoff'/>Find the change between neighbours, and keep adding it.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The next three terms are six point four, six point eight and seven point two.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's idea 6.1 is crossed out; the jump from 5.6 to 6.0 is marked 0.4

marks.jump: the jump from 5.6 to 6.0 is drawn and marked 0.4
marks.fix: 6.1 is crossed out and 6.4 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the next term is six point one, adding one tenth.
<bookmark mark='jump'/>But the jump from five point six to six point zero is four tenths.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Every jump in this pattern is four tenths, so the next term is six point four.
